Article III defines Membership eligibility, admission, and Active/Inactive status. Eligibility for Membership is granted to every person the Vice President determines is an Eligible Employee. Admission to Membership occurs when an Eligible Employee is not a U.S. Person at the relevant time, following Vice President approval, effective as of the Entry Date, with a sufficient period before the Proposed Entry Date to avoid PIRP-DC Accounts being considered deferred compensation under Section 409A of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code. No one is admitted without Vice President approval. A Member is an Active Member during the period they are (a) employed as an Eligible Employee, (b) not a U.S. Person, and (c) currently approved as an Active Member by the Vice President; otherwise, they are an Inactive Member. Article IV outlines Contributions: Pay Credits are allocated to a Member’s PIRP-DC Account based on the Vice President’s determination, with the amount determined by multiplying the Active Member’s annualized Salary as of the Valuation Date by an applicable percentage of 5%, 8%, 10%, 12%, or 18%. For Eligible Employees becoming Active Members on or after January 1, 2021 with no Service completed while a U.S. Person, the Pay Credit is based on “points” calculated as the sum of the Member’s age and years of Service (in whole years and days), with the following point ranges: less than 35 (5%), 35–39 (6%), 40–44 (7%), 45–49 (8%), 50–54 (9%), 55–59 (10%), 60–64 (11%), 65 or more (12%). Otherwise, the applicable percentage is specified by the Vice President at the Member’s Entry Date or upon re-entry as an Active Member, and may be revised annually. Pay Credits are prorated if the Member has less than one full year of Active Membership since the last Valuation Date, with the fractional year calculated by dividing days of Membership or Active Membership by the total days in the Plan Year. A period of paid leave is considered Active Membership for Pay Credit purposes; unpaid leave is not, and thus Pay Credit is prorated or eliminated. In the Member’s final year of Membership, Pay Credit and Interest Credit are determined as of the Distribution Valuation Date with proration based on the fractional final year. Interest Credit is available to Active or Inactive Members who had a PIRP-DC Account balance as of the prior Plan Year’s Valuation Date, calculated by multiplying the Interest Rate for the period since the last Valuation Date by the Account balance as of that date. Pay Credit and Interest Credit are determined by the Vice President as soon as administratively practicable after each Valuation Date, and such determination is conclusive and binding. Section 4.02 allows the Corporation to reduce any payment or benefit by the amount of any obligation to the Corporation or by (a) material benefits accrued under a retirement plan sponsored by the Corporation or any political subdivision, to the extent the Vice President determines the benefit relates to Service or Salary taken into account in Pay Credits, and (b) termination indemnity or other termination-related payments, to the extent the Vice President determines the payment is reasonably related to Service taken into account in Pay Credits. The Corporation may reduce any payment or benefit payable to or on behalf of a Member by the amount of any obligation the Member has to the Corporation, or by the amount of (a) any material benefits accrued by the Member under a retirement plan sponsored by the Corporation or by any country, state, province, or other political subdivision or locality, to the extent the Vice President determines that the benefit amount under such plan relates to Service or Salary that is considered in providing Pay Credits under the DC Program, and (b) any termination indemnity or other payment to the Member by the Employer or PepsiCo Organization related to the Member’s termination of employment, to the extent the Vice President determines that the payment is reasonably related to Service that is taken into account in providing Pay Credits under the DC Program. The Vice President has sole and absolute discretion to determine whether a benefit is material and to apply this Section, with no other party having a right to challenge or override such determination. Pay Credits and Interest Credits are credited to a Member’s PIRP-DC Account as of the Valuation Date to which they relate (or, in the Member’s final year of Membership, as of the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date), or as soon as administratively practicable thereafter. A Member becomes fully vested in and has a nonforfeitable right to their PIRP-DC Account upon completing three years of Service, or earlier upon the Member’s death or disability while employed by the Employer or PepsiCo Organization, with the determination of disability made by the Vice President according to standards deemed appropriate. A Member’s PIRP-DC Account is distributed upon termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization or death, whichever occurs first, in a single lump sum payment on the first of the month following the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date. In the case of disability-related termination, the Vice President determines both the disability and the date of termination. Upon death, the distribution is made on the first day of the month following the Distribution Valuation Date, and if no Dependant is designated or all designated dependants have predeceased the Member, the payment goes to the Member’s Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or to the Member’s estate if neither exists. Interest Credits are credited to the PIRP-DC Account until the Distribution Valuation Date. A Member may designate one or more dependants who will receive benefits upon death, with the right to change or revoke such designation at any time before the effective date, and if the Member is married, any designation of a non-Eligible Spouse requires written consent from the Eligible Spouse; revocation does not require such consent. All designations, changes, revocations, and consents must be in writing, on forms provided by the Vice President, and filed with the Vice President to be effective. The Plan is administered solely by the Vice President, who has the authority to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, and make all determinations in his sole discretion, all of which are final, binding, and conclusive on all parties. The Vice President may delegate responsibilities to other persons or entities, and any reference to the Vice President’s action may refer to a delegate or designated person. If a person entitled to a benefit is legally disabled or incapacitated, the Vice President may direct payments to a legal representative or apply the benefit in a manner deemed advisable, and such payment constitutes a complete discharge of liability. The Vice President has exclusive and absolute discretion to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility, and decide the amount of benefits for any Petitioner, even if such discretion is not expressly granted or required by the Plan, and all decisions are final and binding. The Vice President may consider the Company’s intent in making determinations, and the discretion is intended to be as broad as possible. Decisions are subject to review by a court under the arbitrary and capricious standard. If a claim is denied, the Vice President must provide written notice within 90 days, including the reason(s) for denial, references to relevant Plan provisions, additional material needed to perfect the claim, and a description of the claim review process. If special circumstances require an extension, the period may be extended to 180 days, with notice provided before the end of the initial 90-day period. Upon review, the Petitioner is given the opportunity to submit comments, documents, and records, and the Vice President’s review must consider such submissions, with a final decision made within 60 days (or up to an additional 60 days if extended) and must be in writing, include specific reasons and references to Plan provisions, and provide the Petitioner free access to all relevant documents. Any claim reviewed by a court, arbitrator, or tribunal is limited to the record before the Vice President at the time of the original determination, and exhaustion of rights under this section is required, with no excusal for failure to respond to a claim unless the Petitioner took steps to make it reasonably clear to the Vice President that a claim was being made, or for failure to obtain documents unless (A) the Petitioner is lawfully entitled to them, (B) the request is in writing and received by the Vice President, (C) the documents were not provided within six months (or a reasonable period), (D) the Petitioner made sufficient steps to notify the Vice President of a colorable claim, and (E) the documents are material to one or more colorable claims. Any claim or action related to the Plan must be brought within two years of the date the cause of action accrues, which is the earliest of (i) when the benefits are calculated, (ii) the date identified for payment commencement, (iii) when the Petitioner has actual or constructive knowledge of the basis of the claim, or (iv) when the benefit is first paid or denied. For claims not covered by subsection (a), the two-year period begins when the Petitioner has actual or constructive knowledge of the facts giving rise to the claim. Failure to file within this period precludes any claim, and correspondence under the mandatory appeals process does not extend this period. All claims must be filed in the state or federal courts of New York, specifically the court nearest the Corporation’s headquarters. Specific references to the Vice President’s discretion do not imply that such discretion is less complete or broad in any other context. Specific forms of payment are not protected under this provision. The Corporation’s rights under this Article are as broad as permitted by applicable law. The Plan may be amended from time to time, with or without retroactive effect, subject to Section 8.01. An Employer other than the Corporation does not have the right to amend the Plan. Payments to, for, or in connection with a Member may not exceed the exact amount due as specified in the Plan, including the time and recipient of payment; any excess, premature, or misdirected payment (an “Excess Payment”) must be restored promptly to the Plan. In exchange for receiving an Excess Payment or any direct or indirect right from the Plan, the recipient grants the Plan a constructive trust and first priority equitable lien on any such payment or its proceeds, increased by appropriate interest, and any transfer is subject to this lien; the Plan also has the right to offset such payments to recover the Excess Payment with interest, at the discretion of the Vice President; the Plan may bring equitable or legal actions to enforce these rights, and upon receiving an Excess Payment, the Member waives all rights to any jurisdiction based on present or future residence. The recipient must take all actions requested by the Vice President to recover the Excess Payment. If a Member engages in Prohibited Misconduct prior to the second anniversary of termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization, the Member forfeits all Pay Credits and Interest Credits (whether previously paid, currently paid, or payable in the future), and the PIRP-DC Account is adjusted to reflect such forfeiture, with previously paid amounts recovered. Prohibited Misconduct includes: (1) accepting employment, ownership interest, or responsibility in a business that markets, sells, distributes, or produces “Covered Products” (defined as beverages, juices, dairy products, snacks, hot cereals, pancake mixes, value-added rice and pasta products, ready-to-eat cereals, dry pasta, or any product under development by PepsiCo during employment), unless such business makes retail sales or consumes Covered Products without competing with PepsiCo; (2) soliciting a PepsiCo employee to leave or accept a position with another entity; (3) using or disclosing confidential information about PepsiCo’s customers, suppliers, distributors, business operations, product lines, formulas, pricing, processes, research, financial data, or plans and strategies, except as necessary in the Member’s role; (4) engaging in acts contrary to PepsiCo’s best interests, including violating the Corporation’s Code of Conduct, unlawful trading based on non-public information, or gross misconduct; (5) engaging in fraud. Notwithstanding this, the Plan does not prohibit a Member from communicating with government authorities about possible legal violations without notice, participating in investigations, or receiving awards for such disclosures, and the Corporation retains attorney-client privilege over protected information. The Plan is exempt from Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code, and no Member who is a U.S. Person may have their benefits vest, increase, or be enhanced as a result of compensation or service while a U.S. Person; Interest Credits may be provided on a U.S. Person’s PIRP-DC Account only if the Pay Credits relate to service completed while the Member was not a U.S. Person, and Interest Credits on such Pay Credits. A Member is not entitled to a Benefit Enhancement for a calendar year until it is determined after the year-end that the Member was not a U.S. Person during that year. In the calendar year a Member’s benefit commences, the Vice President may authorize a Benefit Enhancement if it is determined that the Member will not be a U.S. Person during that year; otherwise, the benefit commences without a Benefit Enhancement, and adjustments are made in the following year if the Member was not a U.S. Person during the commencement year. The Pre-409A PepsiCo PEP Document was first effective January 1, 2005 (the "Effective Date") and was restated to reflect amendments through December 31, 2008, generally retaining the 1989 restatement without modification, with clarification that it sets forth the terms of the Plan applicable to benefits earned and vested on or before December 31, 2004 (the "Pre-409A Program"). A 2016 restatement, effective April 1, 2016, reflected amendments through that date, including the merger of the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PBG PEP) into the PEP Plan, effective at the end of the day on December 31, 2011. A Participant is an Employee participating in the Plan under Section 3.1. PBGC is the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation, a body corporate under Title IV of ERISA. The PBGC Rate is 120 percent of the interest rate, determined on the Participant’s Annuity Starting Date, that the PBGC would use to determine the present value of a lump sum distribution on plan termination. A Pension is one or more payments payable to a person entitled to benefits under the Plan; “Pre-409A Pension” refers to the portion derived from the Pre-409A Program, and “409A Pension” refers to the portion derived from the 409A Program. A PEP Election is a Participant’s election to receive a Pre-409A Retirement Pension in one of the annuity forms under Section 6.2, made in compliance with Sections 6.3 and 6.4. The PepsiCo Administration Committee or PAC is responsible for Plan administration and operation, as set forth in the Plan, and as of any time, the Chair is the Company’s Senior Vice President, Total Rewards, or if that position is vacant or eliminated, the person acting to fulfill the majority (or plurality, if no one fulfills a majority) of the duties as they existed prior to the vacancy or elimination. The Chair appoints other PAC members, applying the Guiding Principles and ensuring at least four members with relevant experience, and at least twice a year prepares a written report of significant activities available to any U.S.-based executive who is at least a senior vice president. The PepsiCo Organization is the controlled group of organizations of which PepsiCo, Inc. is a part, as defined by Code section 414 and regulations thereunder, and an entity is a member only during the period it is part of that group. The Plan is the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan, as set forth herein and in the 409A Program document(s), as amended from time to time (subject to applicable amendment limitations). The Plan is also referred to as PEP or the PepsiCo Pension Benefit Equalization Plan. The Plan Administrator is the PAC or its delegate(s), with authority to administer the Plan as provided in Article VII. The Plan Year is the 12-month period from January 1 to December 31. A Post-2004 Participant is any Participant who is not a Pre-2005 Participant. The Pre-409A Program is the program described in this document and any predecessor documents referenced in the Foreword, identifying the portion of the Plan not subject to Section 409A. A Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is the Pension available to an Eligible Spouse under the Plan, and “Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pre-409A Pension” refers to the Pension available to an Eligible Spouse under Section 4.6. A Pre-2005 Participant is one not employed by the PepsiCo Organization after December 31, 2004, whose rights to a Pension are solely based on legally binding rights existing on or before December 31, 2004, and not materially modified after October 3, 2004. The Primary Social Security Amount, for determining Retirement, Vested, or Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension, is the estimated monthly old-age insurance benefit at age 65 under Title II of the Social Security Act, assuming social security wages in any year prior to Retirement or severance equal the Taxable Wage Base in that year and no social security wages are received after Retirement or severance. For a Vested Pension under Formula A of Section 5.2, the estimate assumes continued receipt of social security wages at the Taxable Wage Base rate until age 65. For a Disability Pension, the Primary Social Security Amount is the initial monthly disability insurance benefit received under Title II of the Social Security Act at the time of retirement due to disability, except that for any period before receiving such benefit, the amount is determined under paragraph (1). For paragraphs (1) and (2), the Primary Social Security Amount excludes amounts due to the spouse, dependents, or death, and estimates are based on the Social Security Act as in effect at the Participant’s Severance from Service Date, without regard to subsequent increases in the wage base or benefit levels. A Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity is payable to the Participant for life with 50 percent of the amount payable after the Participant’s death to their surviving Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner for life; if the spouse or domestic partner predeceases the Participant, no survivor benefit is payable. The monthly payment under a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity is reduced as provided in Sections 5.1 and 5.2. Retirement is termination of employment for reasons other than death after fulfilling requirements for a Normal, Early, Late, or Disability Retirement Pension under Article IV. Retirement Date is the day immediately following: (i) the Participant’s last day of employment, or (ii) the last day of an Authorized Leave of Absence, whichever is later. For a Disability Pre-409A Retirement Pension, Retirement commences on the retirement date applicable under the Salaried Plan. A Retirement Pension is payable to a Participant upon Retirement under the Plan; “Pre-409A Retirement Pension” refers to the portion derived from the Pre-409A Program.

A Joint and Survivor Annuity is payable to any person, and the monthly payment amount for a Participant under a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity is reduced to the extent specified in Sections 5.1 and 5.2, as applicable. Retirement occurs when an employee terminates employment for reasons other than death after fulfilling the requirements for a Normal, Early, Late, or Disability Retirement Pension under Article IV. The Retirement Date is the day immediately following either the Participant’s last day of employment or the last day of an Authorized Leave of Absence, whichever is later. However, for a Disability Pre-409A Retirement Pension, Retirement is considered to commence on the Participant’s retirement date applicable under the Salaried Plan. A Retirement Pension is the benefit paid to a Participant upon Retirement under the Plan. The term “Pre-409A Retirement Pension” refers to the portion of a Retirement Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program, while “409A Retirement Pension” refers to the portion derived from the 409A Program. The Salaried Plan is the pension program set forth in Part B of the PSERP Component of the PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan A (“PERP-A”), PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan I (“PERP-I”), and PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan H (“PERP-H”), as amended from time to time and as it existed prior to January 1, 2017 in predecessor plans to PERP-A and PERP-I. Section 409A refers to Section 409A of the Code. Service is the period of a Participant’s employment calculated in accordance with Section 3.2 for determining benefit entitlement. A 75 Percent Survivor Annuity is payable to the Participant for life, with 75 percent of the amount paid to the Participant’s surviving Eligible Spouse for life after the Participant’s death; if the Eligible Spouse predeceases the Participant, no survivor benefit is payable. The monthly payment under a 75 Percent Survivor Annuity is also reduced to the extent provided in Sections 5.1 and 5.2, as applicable. The Severance from Service Date is the date when an Employee’s period of service is deemed to end, as determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan. A Single Life Annuity is a level monthly annuity payable to a Participant for his life only, with no survivor benefits. A Single Lump Sum is the distribution of a Participant’s total Pre-409A Pension in a single payment. The Social Security Act refers to the Social Security Act of the United States, as amended, providing governmental benefits for old age, death, and disability; any reference to it or its benefits shall be interpreted as a reference to a comparable governmental program in another country, as determined by the Plan Administrator, only if such computation is administratively feasible. The Taxable Wage Base is the contribution and benefit base (as determined under section 230 of the Social Security Act) in effect for the Plan Year. A Vested Pension is the Pension available to a Participant under Section 4.3; “Pre-409A Vested Pension” refers to the portion derived from the Pre-409A Program, and “409A Vested Pension” refers to the portion derived from the 409A Program. The terms of the Plan are construed in accordance with Section 2.2, which includes rules on gender and number, compounds of “here,” examples, and the structure of the document, which is organized into articles, sections, subsections, paragraphs, subparagraphs, clauses, and sub-clauses. Article III outlines Participation and Service: an Employee is a Participant during the period when they would be entitled to a Pension if employment terminated at that time or would be entitled but for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7; entitlement is subject to exclusions from eligibility under the Salaried Plan. Service is determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan. Credited Service is the period used to determine the amount of a Participant’s Pension or a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension, as determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan. Article IV outlines the requirements for benefits: a Participant is eligible for a Normal Pre-409A Retirement Pension if they meet the requirements in Section 4.1 of the Salaried Plan as of December 31, 2004, with no changes after the Effective Date taken into account; the Participant’s status under this section is fixed as of December 31, 2004. Similarly, eligibility for an Early Pre-409A Retirement Pension is based on meeting the requirements in Section 4.2 of the Salaried Plan as of December 31, 2004, with no changes after the Effective Date. A Participant who is vested under Section 4.7 and terminates employment before being eligible for a Normal or Early Pre-409A Retirement Pension is eligible for a Pre-409A Vested Pension, with no changes after the Effective Date taken into account; the Participant’s status under this section is fixed as of December 31, 2004. A Participant who terminates employment before satisfying the vesting requirement in Section 4.7 is not eligible for a Pension under the Plan. A Late Pre-409A Retirement Pension is available after a Participant continues employment past their Normal Retirement Age, with eligibility determined under Section 4.4 of the Salaried Plan, excluding any changes after the Effective Date, any requirement for notice under ERISA section 203(a)(3)(B), and any adjustment under Section 5.7(d) of the Salaried Plan; the Participant’s status under this section is fixed as of December 31, 2004. A Participant is eligible for a Pre-409A Disability Retirement Pension if they meet the requirements for a Disability Retirement Pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan, with no changes after the Effective Date taken into account; the Participant’s status under this section is fixed as of December 31, 2004. A Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pre-409A Pension is payable only if the Participant dies before their Annuity Starting Date and commences at the same time as the corresponding pre-retirement spouse’s pension under the Salaried Plan, with no changes after the Effective Date taken into account, subject to Section 4.9. For active, disabled, and retired employees, the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pre-409A Pension is payable to an Eligible Spouse entitled under the Salaried Plan to a pre-retirement spouse’s pension, but only if the Participant died after December 31, 2004 and met the eligibility requirements for a Retirement Pension on that date. For vested employees, the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pre-409A Pension is payable to an Eligible Spouse entitled under the Salaried Plan to a pre-retirement spouse’s pension for survivors of vested terminated employees, but only if the Participant died after December 31, 2004 and met the requirements for a Vested Pension but not a Retirement Pension on that date. If such coverage is in effect, any Pension calculated under Section 5.2(b) is reduced by an applicable percentage based on the Participant’s age at the time of coverage, with a pro rata reduction for partial years, and no reduction applies for coverage within 90 days of termination of employment. The applicable age-based annual charges are: up to 35 years – 0.0%, 35–39 – 0.075%, 40–44 – 0.1%, 45–49 – 0.175%, 50–54 – 0.3%, 55–59 – 0.5%, 60–64 – 0.5%. A Participant becomes fully vested in their Accrued Benefit at the time they become fully vested under the Salaried Plan. The distribution of a Participant’s Pre-409A Pension commences as specified in Section 6.1. Any interest increase due to a delay in payment, calculated under Section 3.1(e) of Part A of the Salaried Plan, accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid at the same time and in the same form as the Participant’s 409A Pension, with the interest adjustment limited to the amount that may be paid under the 409A Pension, consistent with Section 409A’s payment rules. A Participant does not receive interest for a delay in payment of their 409A or Pre-409A Pension if the delay is caused by the Participant. For certain small benefit annuity payments, a Participant may receive a cashout: if on the applicable benefit commencement date the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value of the Pre-409A Pension is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator distributes the lump sum value. For commencement dates prior to December 1, 2012, a Participant is cashed out if the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value is equal to or less than $15,000 ($10,000 for a Pre-2005 Participant). The applicable benefit commencement date is: (1) prior to December 1, 2012, the commencement date of any 409A Pension to which the Participant is entitled, or if not entitled to a 409A Pension, the first of the month following the Participant’s termination of employment date, provided that if the lump sum value as of that date is too low, the distribution may be adjusted accordingly.

If the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value of a Participant’s Pre-409A Pension is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator shall distribute such lump sum value to the Participant. For commencement dates prior to December 1, 2012, a Participant shall be cashed out if the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value is equal to or less than $15,000 ($10,000 for a Pre-2005 Participant). The applicable benefit commencement date is: (1) prior to December 1, 2012, the commencement date of any 409A Pension to which the Participant is entitled, or if not entitled, the first of the month following the Participant’s termination of employment date (with the exception that if the lump sum value as of that date is too great to make the distribution but not too great as of the Annuity Starting Date under the Pre-409A Program, then the Annuity Starting Date becomes the applicable commencement date); and (2) beginning on December 1, 2012, the first of the month following the Participant’s termination of employment date (with the same exception regarding the Annuity Starting Date). For the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pre-409A Pension, if the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit on the Eligible Spouse’s applicable benefit commencement date, the Eligible Spouse shall receive such lump sum value. For commencement dates prior to December 1, 2012, an Eligible Spouse shall be cashed out if the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value is equal to or less than $15,000 ($10,000 for a Pre-2005 Participant). The applicable benefit commencement date is: (1) prior to December 1, 2012, the commencement date of any Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension to which the Eligible Spouse is entitled, or if not entitled, the first of the month following the Participant’s death (with the exception that if the lump sum value as of that date is too great to make the distribution but not too great as of the date that would be the Eligible Spouse’s benefit commencement date under the Pre-409A Program, then that date becomes the applicable commencement date); and (2) beginning on December 1, 2012, the first of the month following the Participant’s death (with the same exception). The Plan Administrator has discretion to cash out a Pre-409A Vested Pension in a single lump sum prior to the date that would apply under subsection (a). As of December 1, 2012, any Pre-409A Vested Pension that has not had its Annuity Starting Date occur, has an Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value equal to or less than the Cashout Limit, and is practicable to calculate and distribute may be cashed out on December 1, 2012. As of the first day of any month in 2013 or 2014 specified by the Plan Administrator, any such Vested Pension may be cashed out on that specified date, provided it meets the same conditions. Not later than November 30, the Plan Administrator must create a written list (in hard copy or electronic form) of Participants with Pre-409A Vested Pensions to be cashed out on December 1, 2012. Not later than the day before the specified date in paragraph (2), a similar written list must be created for cashouts on that date. Any lump sum distributed under this section shall be in lieu of the Pension that would otherwise be distributable to the Participant or Eligible Spouse. To preserve the grandfathered status of Pre-409A Pensions, the cashout provisions in subsections (a) through (c) are intended to operate in conformance with the rules for “limited cashout” features under Treasury Regulation sections 1.409A-3(j)(4)(v) and 1.409A-6(a)(4)(i)(E), and shall be interpreted and applied consistently with these regulations. No Participant or Eligible Spouse shall be given a direct or indirect election regarding whether their Vested Pension or the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension will be cashed out. In the case of a current or former Participant who is reemployed and eligible to reparticipate in the Salaried Plan after their Annuity Starting Date, payment of their Pre-409A Pension will be suspended if payment of their Salaried Plan pension is suspended (or would have been suspended if it were already in pay status and changes in Salaried Plan terms after December 31, 2004 were disregarded). Thereafter, their Pre-409A Pension shall recommence at the time determined under Section 6.1, even if the suspension of their Salaried Plan pension ends earlier. When a Pension becomes payable to or on behalf of a Post-2004 Participant under this Plan, the amount of such Pre-409A Pension shall be determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3 (whichever is applicable), subject to any adjustments required under Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5. For a Pre-2005 Participant, the amount of such Participant’s Pre-409A Pension (or a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pre-409A Pension payable on his behalf) shall be determined as provided in Article B of the Appendix. A Post-2004 Participant’s Pre-409A Pension is calculated as the greater of (1) the present value method, which determines the present value of the Participant’s benefit as of December 31, 2004, using the 2004 Lump Sum Factors, adjusted for interest and survivorship through the Earliest Date, or (2) the Accrued Benefit Method, which bases the amount on the Participant’s Accrued Benefit as of December 31, 2004, reduced for early commencement based on the Participant’s actual Annuity Starting Date, using applicable early commencement reduction factors, but never exceeding the Participant’s Total Pension reduced by their Salaried Plan Pension, calculated as of the actual Annuity Starting Date. For purposes of this calculation, the Total Pension is the greater of (i) the amount of the Participant’s pension under the Salaried Plan without regard to limitations under sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code or actuarial adjustments under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan, or (ii) the amount of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2, all determined as of December 31, 2004 and based on the terms of the Salaried Plan without considering changes after that date. A Participant’s Salaried Plan Pension is determined as of December 31, 2004, and without regard to changes after that date, except for early commencement reductions which are made as of the Annuity Starting Date. A Post-2004 Participant who has 1988 pensionable earnings from an Employer of at least $75,000 is eligible for a PEP Guarantee benefit. “1988 pensionable earnings” means the Participant’s remuneration for the 1988 calendar year under the Salaried Plan as in effect in 1988, excluding remuneration from an entity attributable to any period when that entity was not an Employer. The PEP Guarantee amount is determined under the applicable formula in paragraph (1), subject to special rules in paragraph (2). Formula A provides a Pension amount equal to 3 percent of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus 1 percent of the Highest Average Monthly Earnings for each year of Credited Service in excess of 10 years, less 1-2/3 percent of the Participant’s Primary Social Security Amount multiplied by years of Credited Service not in excess of 30 years. For a Vested Pension under Formula A, the amount is first calculated based on Credited Service the Participant would have earned had they remained employed until their Normal Retirement Age, and their Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Primary Social Security Amount at their Severance from Service Date, then reduced by multiplying the resulting amount by a fraction where the numerator is the Participant’s actual years of Credited Service on their Severance from Service Date (or December 31, 2004, if earlier) and the denominator is the years of Credited Service they would have earned had they remained employed until their Normal Retirement Age. Formula B provides the greater of (A) 1-1/2 percent of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times the number of years of Credited Service, less 50 percent of the Participant’s Primary Social Security Amount, or (B) 3 percent of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times the number of years of Credited Service up to 15 years, less 50 percent of the Participant’s Primary Social Security Amount. In determining the amount of a Disability Pension under Formula A or B, the Pension shall be calculated on the basis of the Participant’s Credited Service and earnings.

The Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) Guarantee under the Pre-409A Program is calculated based on the Participant’s Credited Service as of their Severance from Service Date (or December 31, 2004, if earlier), with the amount reduced by multiplying the resulting figure by a fraction where the numerator is the Participant’s actual years of Credited Service on their Severance from Service Date and the denominator is the years of Credited Service they would have earned had they remained employed until their Normal Retirement Age. The Pension amount under Formula B is the greater of (A) 1-1/2 percent of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings multiplied by the number of years of Credited Service, less 50 percent of the Participant’s Primary Social Security Amount, or (B) 3 percent of the Highest Average Monthly Earnings times the number of years of Credited Service up to 15 years, less 50 percent of the Primary Social Security Amount. For Disability Pensions under Formula A or B, the calculation is based on the Participant’s Credited Service (as defined in Section 3.3(d)(3) of the Salaried Plan as of December 31, 2004), their Highest Average Monthly Earnings, and Primary Social Security Amount at the date of disability (or an earlier applicable date under Section 5.1(b)). The PEP Guarantee amount is subject to special rules: (i) if the Participant has an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, the spouse or partner is entitled to a survivor annuity equal to 50 percent of the Participant’s Annuity, with no reduction in the Participant’s Annuity, and if the surviving spouse or partner is more than 10 years younger than the Participant, the survivor benefit is reduced by 0.8 percent for each full year between 10 and 20, and by an additional 0.4 percent for each full year over 20; (ii) reductions apply if the Participant receives an Early Retirement Pension (reduced by 3/12ths of 1 percent per month before the Normal Retirement Date), if the Participant has a Vested Pension (reduced to the Actuarial Equivalent of the Normal Retirement Date benefit if payment begins earlier, with Section 4.6(b) reductions for Pre-Retirement Spouse’s coverage), if the Participant receives a survivor annuity for a beneficiary who is not an Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner (reduced to the Actuarial Equivalent of a Single Life Annuity for the Participant’s life), if the Pension includes inflation protection (reduced to the Actuarial Equivalent of the annuity without inflation protection), or if the Pension is distributed as a lump sum (adjusted to the Actuarial Equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, including any survivor benefit and early retirement reductions). The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pre-409A Pension is determined by subtracting the Eligible Spouse’s Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension from the Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension, which is the greater of (i) the pre-retirement spouse’s pension under Section 5.1(b) and the Salaried Plan in effect on December 31, 2004, without regard to limitations under sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code or actuarial adjustments under Section 5.7(d), or (ii) the PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension determined under paragraph (1) or (2) below. The PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is determined under the Normal Rule: if the Participant had separated from service on the earliest of the date of death or their actual Severance from Service Date, commenced a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity on the same date as the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension commencement, and died the day after commencement, the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension would be the amount payable under such annuity, with early commencement reductions applied if payment begins before the Normal Retirement Date; or under the Special Rule for Active and Disabled Employees: the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension shall not be less than 25 percent of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee (as determined under Section 5.2) if a comparable 25 percent benefit is available under the Salaried Plan, and this benefit is not reduced for early commencement. Pensions are subject to adjustment: (a) for rehired Participants, the Pre-409A Pension is recalculated when the Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated due to additional Credited Service, with the PEP Guarantee adjusted similarly to the Salaried Plan benefits; (b) if a benefit under a specified plan (defined as the Salaried Plan or a nonqualified pension plan sponsored by PepsiCo and not based on participant pay deferrals) is increased after the PEP benefit is determined, the PEP benefit is recalculated, and any overpayment is recovered as deemed appropriate, with no duplication of payments. Excludable Employment applies to executives classified as level 22 or above (or equivalent) with limited-duration assignments effective from June 30, 1997, who are not entitled to benefits or increases from such employment; additionally, for agreements entered into after January 1, 2009, executives who waive eligibility or agree not to participate in the Plan under a written agreement are not entitled to benefits or increases from such employment, and such agreements are irrevocable once executed. Distribution options for Pre-409A Pensions begin on or after March 1, 1992, and are governed by this Article, with distributions before that date following prior Plan terms; unless otherwise provided in Section 4.9 (cashout distributions), Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pensions are payable as an annuity for the life of the Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner. For distributions beginning on or after March 1, 1992: (a) if a Participant does not have an Advance Election in effect as of the close of business on the day before Retirement or terminates employment prior to Retirement, the Pre-409A Pension is paid in the same form and at the same time as the Salaried Plan Pension, with payment beginning on the first month after Severance from Service Date if the Salaried Plan Annuity Starting Date occurs while still employed, and if the Salaried Plan offers a form of payment not available under the Pre-409A Program, the form is determined under subsection (b)(2); (b) if a Participant has an Advance Election in effect, the Pre-409A Pension is paid as a Single Lump Sum if an Advance Election to receive a Single Lump Sum is in effect, or as an Annuity beginning on the first month after Retirement Date if an Advance Election to receive an Annuity is in effect. For an Annuity, if the Participant has a qualifying Salaried Plan election (a written election in effect as of the close of business on the day before Retirement that specifies an Annuity for all or part of the Retirement Pension), the distribution form matches the Salaried Plan election; if the Participant has a PEP Election, the distribution form matches the selected Annuity in the PEP Election; if the Participant has no such election, the form is not specified.

A Participant’s Pre-409A Retirement Pension distribution is determined based on the form of payment selected under specific conditions. If a Participant makes a qualifying Salaried Plan election—defined as a written election, in effect as of the day before retirement, specifying an Annuity for all or part of the pension—the distribution will be in the form of that Annuity. A Participant who elects a combination of lump sum and Annuity is considered to have selected an Annuity for part of the pension. If not covered by the above, and if the Participant has a PEP Election in effect as of the day before retirement, the distribution will be in the form of the Annuity selected in that election. If neither a qualifying Salaried Plan election nor a PEP Election is in effect, the distribution will be a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the Participant is married, or a Single Life Annuity if unmarried, with marriage determined as of the day before retirement. The available forms of payment include: (1) a Single Life Annuity, which provides monthly payments ending before the Participant’s death; (2) survivor options—100 percent, 75 percent, or 50 percent—where payments continue to a beneficiary after the Participant’s death, with the 50 percent option being a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the beneficiary is an Eligible Spouse; (3) a Ten Years Certain and Life Option, which provides payments for at least 120 months, with any unpaid amounts going to a primary or contingent beneficiary if the Participant dies before 120 payments; and (4) a Single Lump Sum or a Combination Lump Sum/Monthly Benefit Option, where the pension is split based on percentages designated by the Participant, with the lump sum amount calculated by multiplying the full lump sum amount by the designated percentage and the monthly benefit amount calculated by multiplying the elected monthly benefit by the designated percentage. Inflation protection of 5% or 7% may be elected, with benefits increasing if inflation exceeds the selected threshold, measured over the 12-month period ending September 30, and adjustments beginning on the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date; such protection applies to survivor benefits and is irrevocable. For vested benefits, married Participants may choose a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity or a 75 Percent Survivor Annuity, while all Participants (married or unmarried) may receive a Single Life Annuity. Advance Elections must be in writing, on a designated form, signed by the Participant, and submitted before the start of the calendar year containing retirement and at least 6 months prior to retirement, remaining effective until changed or revoked; revocations must also meet the same timing requirements. A PEP Election may only be made by a Participant who has an Advance Election in effect, and the Advance Election’s receipt requirement is considered met if it will be met by the proposed retirement date. The PEP Election must be submitted no earlier than 180 days (90 days prior to January 1, 2007) before retirement and no later than the close of business on the day before retirement, and the Participant must provide proof of the beneficiary’s age by the day before retirement for any payment subject to reduction under Section 6.2(c). A PEP Election becomes effective at the close of business on the day before retirement and is void if no Advance Election is in effect. For participants rehired after their initial Annuity Starting Date and who were receiving an Annuity upon rehire or had previously received a lump sum distribution (other than a cashout), only the portion of the benefit accruing after rehire is subject to the election procedures at the subsequent Annuity Starting Date, with prior accruals continuing under the initial election. An election is considered received on a given day if it is postmarked that day or actually received by the Plan Administrator by close of business, as determined by the Plan Administrator. If a Participant makes a PEP Election for a survivor option and dies before the election becomes effective, the election is disregarded; if the Participant dies after the election becomes effective but before pension commencement, payments begin to the surviving Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner, or other beneficiary on the first day of the month following death, with any back payments going to the estate. If a Participant dies after the election becomes effective, without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and before receiving 120 payments under the Ten Years Certain and Life Option, the remaining payments go to the estate; if a beneficiary dies before payments are completed, the remaining payments go to the beneficiary’s estate. If a Participant’s beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, the Participant may not elect the 100 percent survivor option if the beneficiary is more than 10 years younger, or the 75 percent survivor option if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger. A Participant who elects a survivor option must designate a beneficiary on a PEP Election Form or an approved Salaried Plan form, with the ability to name both a primary and contingent beneficiary under the 50 percent survivor option; the designation may be changed or revoked at any time before the election becomes effective, and is only effective upon filing with the Plan Administrator. If no beneficiary is properly designated, the survivor option is not effective. A Participant entitled to a Pre-409A Vested Pension cannot name a beneficiary; if such a participant elects an optional form of payment, the beneficiary is their Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date. A portion of a Participant’s Pre-409A Pension may be paid as a single lump sum to satisfy FICA and related income taxes, with any shortfall in the 409A Pension being offset by a portion of the Pre-409A Pension if the 409A Pension has not commenced when taxes are due.

The Plan shall be administered by the Plan Administrator, which has the authority to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, maintain records, perform benefit calculations, and rely on information provided by the Participant, such as current mailing address, age, and marital status. The Plan Administrator’s interpretations, determinations, regulations, and calculations are final and binding on all parties. Neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is considered a fiduciary under the Plan, and restrictions under section 406 of ERISA do not apply to either. If a person entitled to a benefit is under a legal disability or incapacitated, the Plan Administrator may make payments to the person or their legal representative or apply the payment for the person’s benefit, and such payments will fully discharge any liability under the Plan. The Plan Administrator has exclusive discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility, and decide benefit amounts, with no limitations on that discretion—even if not expressly granted or required by the Plan. All decisions are final, conclusive, and binding, and the Plan Administrator may consider the Company’s intent in making determinations, even if such intent is not explicitly stated. The Plan Administrator’s discretion is absolute and intended to be as broad as possible, and any exercise of that discretion will be reviewed by a court under the arbitrary and capricious standard (i.e., abuse of discretion). If a claim for benefits is wholly or partially denied, the Plan Administrator will provide the claimant with a claims review process within 90 days, including specific reasons for denial, references to pertinent Plan provisions, information necessary to perfect the claim, and a description of the review procedure, including time limits and the right to bring a civil action under ERISA after further denial. If special circumstances require an extension, the response period may be extended from 90 to 180 days, with notice provided before the end of the initial 90-day period. A further review is available within 60 days of receiving notice of denial, during which the claimant may submit comments, documents, records, and other relevant information, and the Plan Administrator will consider such submissions regardless of whether they were previously considered. The decision on review will be made within 60 days, with a possible extension of up to an additional 60 days if circumstances warrant it, and notice of such extension will be provided before the end of the initial 60-day period. The final decision must be in writing, clearly understandable, and include specific reasons and references to the relevant Plan provisions. Any review by a court, arbitrator, or other tribunal will be limited to the record before the Plan Administrator at the time of the initial determination, and the claimant must first fully exhaust all rights under the claims procedures before filing in court. The exhaustion requirement applies in all circumstances, including where other disputes are more significant, to any rights the Plan Administrator may provide, regardless of whether they are actual or potential, and even if specific procedures have not been previously established. The Plan Administrator may make special arrangements to consider claims on a class basis or address unusual conflicts, and such arrangements are necessary to ensure exhaustion. Exhaustion is not excused for failure to respond to a claim unless the claimant took steps to make it reasonably clear to the Plan Administrator that a claim was being submitted, or for failure to fulfill a request for documents unless (A) the claimant is lawfully entitled to receive the documents at the time and in the form requested, (B) the request is in writing and received by the Plan Administrator, (C) the documents are not provided within six months (or a reasonable longer period), (D) the claimant took steps to make it reasonably clear they were entitled to the documents, and (E) the documents are material to one or more colorable claims the claimant has informed the Plan Administrator about. For this Section, a “Dispute” includes any claim, dispute, issue, action, or other matter, and a “Claim” includes any Dispute that relates to the interpretation of the Plan, its terms or conditions, applicable law, validity of adoption, administration, violation of ERISA or other law, request for benefits, breach of fiduciary duty, or any claim deemed similar or related to the Plan. A “Claimant” includes any Employee, former Employee, Participant, former Participant, beneficiary, spouse, former spouse, estate, heir, representative, or any other individual or entity with a relationship to such individuals or the Plan, or a group of such individuals. Any claim or action alleging wrongful denial of benefits or interference with ERISA-protected rights must be brought within two years of the date the cause of action first accrues, which is deemed to occur not later than the earliest of (i) when the benefit calculation is received, (ii) the date identified by the Plan Administrator for payment commencement, (iii) when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the basis of the claim, or (iv) when the benefit was first paid or denied. For claims involving interference with ERISA-protected rights, the cause of action accrues when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged interference. For any other claim, the cause of action must be brought within two years of when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the facts giving rise to the claim. Failure to file within this two-year period will preclude any claim or action, and correspondence or communications following the mandatory appeals process do not affect this time frame. Any claim or action related to the Plan must be brought only in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, effective for claims filed on or after January 1, 2011. The PEP Guarantee amount is determined using the applicable formula in paragraph (1), subject to special rules in paragraph (2). Formula A provides a pension equal to 3 percent of the Pre-2005 Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus 1 percent for each year of Credited Service beyond 10 years, less 1-2/3 percent of their Primary Social Security Amount multiplied by years of Credited Service not exceeding 30 years. For a Vested Pension under Formula A, the amount is first calculated based on the Credited Service the participant would have earned had they remained employed until their Normal Retirement Age, using their Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Primary Social Security Amount at their Severance from Service Date, then reduced by multiplying the result by a fraction with the numerator being the actual years of Credited Service on Severance and the denominator being the years of Credited Service they would have earned had they remained employed until Normal Retirement Age. Formula B provides the greater of (A) 1-1/2 percent of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times years of Credited Service, less 50 percent of the Primary Social Security Amount, or (B) 3 percent of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times years of Credited Service up to 15 years, less 50 percent of the Primary Social Security Amount. The PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) was established to benefit salaried employees of the PBG Organization who participate in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan (Salaried Plan), providing pension benefits for employees whose benefits under the Salaried Plan are limited by the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or based on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula.
