The Plan Administrator must memorialize in writing by November 30 the selection of Vested Pensions for cashout on December 1, 2012, through a written list (in hard copy or electronic form), and by the day before the specified date in 2013 or 2014, the selection for cashout on that date. Any lump sum distributed under Section 4.9 replaces the otherwise distributable Pension. The cashout provisions are intended to conform with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(v) and §1.409A-6(a)(4)(i)(E) and shall be interpreted and applied consistently with those regulations. No Participant or Eligible Spouse may make a direct or indirect election regarding whether their Vested Pension or Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension will be cashed out. The terms of this section apply despite prior provisions: prior to April 14, 1991, a Participant is not eligible for a Normal, Early, Vested, or Disability Pension during any month or period for which they are receiving benefits under a long-term disability plan maintained by an Employer; however, the Eligible Spouse is not ineligible for a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity because the Participant was receiving long-term disability benefits at the time of death. If a current or former Participant is reemployed and eligible to reparticipate in the Salaried Plan after their Annuity Starting Date, their Pension will be suspended if their Salaried Plan pension is suspended (or would have been suspended if already in payment), and will recommence at the time determined under Section 6.1, even if the suspension of the Salaried Plan pension ends earlier. Article V determines the amount of the retirement Pension under Section 5.1, 5.2, or 5.3, subject to adjustments under Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5. Section 5.1 defines the PEP Pension: if the Pension is paid in the same form and at the same time as under the Salaried Plan, the Pension is the difference between the Participant’s Total Pension and their Salaried Plan Pension in that form and time. If the form or timing differs, the Pension is the product of the amount of the Total Pension in the applicable form and time, multiplied by a fraction where the numerator is the value of the Total Pension reduced by the value of the Salaried Plan Pension, and the denominator is the value of the Total Pension, with value determined reasonably and consistently by the Plan Administrator for similarly situated employees. A Participant’s “Total Pension” is the greater of (i) the amount of their pension under the Salaried Plan without regard to limitations under sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code or the actuarial adjustment under Section 5.6(d) of Part C of the Salaried Plan, or (ii) the amount of their PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2. When comparing, benefits are calculated for the specific form and time of payment; if the form is a lump sum, Actuarial Equivalent factors from Section 2 of Article II apply instead of those in the Salaried Plan. A Participant’s “Salaried Plan Pension” is the amount of their pension under the Salaried Plan. Section 5.2 covers the PEP Guarantee: a Participant is eligible if they have 1988 pensionable earnings of at least $75,000 from an Employer, where “1988 pensionable earnings” refers to remuneration for the 1988 calendar year recognized for benefits under the Salaried Plan in effect in 1988, excluding remuneration from entities not acting as Employers during those periods. The PEP Guarantee amount is determined under the applicable formula in paragraph (1), subject to special rules in paragraph (2). The formula is: (i) Formula A: the Pension is 3% of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus 1% of the Highest Average Monthly Earnings for each year of Credited Service beyond 10 years, less 1-2/3% of the Participant’s Primary Social Security Amount multiplied by years of Credited Service not exceeding 30 years. For a Vested Pension under Formula A, the Pension is first calculated based on the Credited Service the Participant would have earned had they remained employed by the Employer.

A participant eligible for the Salaried Plan prior to July 1, 1975, receives a Pension under this paragraph equal to the greater of the amounts calculated under subparagraphs (i) and (ii), with the exception that subparagraph (ii)(B) does not apply when determining a Vested Pension. Under Formula A, the Pension is calculated as 3 percent of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus 1 percent of the Highest Average Monthly Earnings for each year of Credited Service beyond 10 years, less 1-2/3 percent of the Participant’s Primary Social Security Amount multiplied by years of Credited Service not exceeding 30 years. For a Vested Pension under Formula A, the amount is first calculated using (I) the Credited Service the Participant would have earned had he remained employed until his Normal Retirement Age, (II) his Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Primary Social Security Amount at his Severance from Service Date, and then reduced by multiplying the result by a fraction where the numerator is the Participant’s actual years of Credited Service at Severance and the denominator is the years of Credited Service he would have earned had he remained employed until Normal Retirement Age. Under Formula B, the Pension is the greater of (A) 1-1/2 percent of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times years of Credited Service, less 50 percent of the Primary Social Security Amount, or (B) 3 percent of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times years of Credited Service up to 15 years, less 50 percent of the Primary Social Security Amount. For Disability Pensions under Formula A or B, the Pension is calculated based on the Participant’s Credited Service (as defined in Section 3.3(d)(3) of Part C of the Salaried Plan), and their Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Primary Social Security Amount at the date of disability. The amount of the PEP Guarantee is determined under paragraph (1) with the following special rules: (i) If the Participant has an Eligible Spouse and has commenced receipt of an Annuity, the spouse is entitled to a survivor annuity equal to 50 percent of the Participant’s Annuity, with no reduction in the Participant’s Annuity, beginning on the first day of the month coincident with or following the Participant’s death and ending with the last monthly payment due prior to the spouse’s death; if the spouse is more than 10 years younger, the survivor benefit is reduced by 0.8 percent for each full year between 10 and 20, and by an additional 0.4 percent for each full year over 20; (ii) Reductions apply as follows: (A) For Early Retirement Pension, the payment is reduced by 3/12ths of 1 percent for each month the benefit commencement date precedes the Normal Retirement Date; (B) For a Vested Pension, the payment is reduced to the Actuarial Equivalent of the amount payable at Normal Retirement Date if payment begins before that date, and Section 4.6(b) reductions for Pre-Retirement Spouse’s coverage apply; (C) If the Pension provides a life annuity for a beneficiary who is not the Eligible Spouse, the Pension is reduced so the total value equals the Actuarial Equivalent of a Single Life Annuity for the Participant’s life; (D) If the Pension includes inflation protection as described in Section 6.2(b), the Pension is reduced so the total value equals the Actuarial Equivalent of the annuity without such protection; (iii) For a lump sum distribution, the Retirement Pension amount is the Actuarial Equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, taking into account any survivor benefit under (i) and any early retirement reductions under (ii)(A). The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is the difference between (1) the Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension and (2) the Eligible Spouse’s Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension. The Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is the greater of (i) the amount under the Salaried Plan without regard to limitations under sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code or the actuarial adjustment under Section 5.6(d) of Part C of the Salaried Plan, or (ii) the amount of the Eligible Spouse’s PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension as determined under subsection (c). The PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is determined under paragraph (1) or (2), whichever applies, with reference to the PEP Guarantee that would have been available to the Participant under Section 5.2. Under the Normal Rule, the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension equals the amount payable as a survivor annuity under a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the Participant had separated from service on the date of death (or earlier, if that date is before the actual Severance from Service Date), commenced the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity on the same date as the start of the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension, and died the day after commencement; if payment begins before the Normal Retirement Date, appropriate reductions for early commencement apply. Under the Special Rule for Active and Disabled Employees, the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is not less than 25 percent of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee determined under Section 5.2, with Credited Service determined as in Section 3.3(d)(2) of Part C of the Salaried Plan, and the deceased Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Primary Social Security Amount, and Covered Compensation determined as of his date of death; this pension is not reduced for early commencement. Pensions are subject to adjustment as provided in Section 5.4. A “specified plan” means the Salaried Plan or a nonqualified pension plan similar to this Plan sponsored by a member of the PBG Organization and not based on participant pay deferrals (including the PepsiCo Prior Plan). For rehired participants, if the Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated based on additional Credited Service, the Pre-409A Pension is recalculated in the same manner as Salaried Plan benefits, adjusting for in-service and prior distributions under this Plan and any specified plans. If a benefit under a specified plan is increased after PEP benefits are determined, the PEP benefit is recalculated; if an overpayment is identified, the Plan Administrator takes steps to recover it, with no duplication of payments under this Plan and any specified plans. Effective June 30, 1997, an executive classified at level 22 or above with a limited duration assignment is not entitled to a benefit or increase in benefits from such employment. Article VI governs the distribution of benefits to a Participant entitled to a Pension under the Plan. For distributions beginning on or after March 1, 1992, Section 6.1 governs form and timing, with prior distributions governed by the Prior Plan. A Participant without an Advance Election in effect as of the close of business on the day before Retirement or who terminates employment prior to Retirement receives the Pension in the same form and at the same time as under the Salaried Plan; if the Salaried Plan Annuity Starting Date occurs while still employed, payment begins on the first month after Severance from Service, and the form remains the same. A Participant with an Advance Election in effect as of the close of business on the day before Retirement and whose Retirement Date is after 1993 receives a Single Lump Sum if such election is in effect, or an Annuity beginning on the first month coincident with or following Retirement. For an Annuity, if the Participant has a qualifying Salaried Plan election (a written election in effect under the Salaried Plan as of the day before Retirement specifying an Annuity for all or part of the Pension), the distribution is in the same form as selected; if the Participant has a PEP Election, the distribution is in the form selected in that election; if neither, the distribution is a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if married or a Single Life Annuity if not married, with marriage determined on the day before Retirement. The available forms of payment are set out in subsection (a) and (b), with the form determined by Section 6.1, payments commencing on the date specified in Section 6.1 and ending on the date specified in this subsection. The forms include a Single Life Annuity (monthly payments ending with the last payment due prior to death), and survivor options: (i) 100 percent Survivor Option (reduced Pension for life, continuing to a beneficiary for life after death), or (ii) 75 percent Survivor Option (reduced Pension for life, with 75 percent of the reduced amount continuing to a beneficiary for life after death).

The pension benefits shall commence on the date specified in Section 6.1 and shall end on the date specified in this subsection. A Participant may receive his Pension as a Single Life Annuity, which provides monthly payments ending with the last payment due prior to his death. Alternatively, the Participant may choose one of the following survivor options: (i) 100 percent Survivor Option, where the Participant receives a reduced Pension for life, with payments continuing at the same reduced amount to a beneficiary for life, beginning on the first day of the month coincident with or following the Participant’s death and ending with the last monthly payment due prior to the beneficiary’s death; (ii) 75 percent Survivor Option, where the Participant receives a reduced Pension for life, and payments of 75 percent of that reduced amount continue to the beneficiary for life under the same conditions; (iii) 50 percent Survivor Option, where the Participant receives a reduced Pension for life, and payments of 50 percent of that reduced amount continue to the beneficiary for life under the same conditions, and this option constitutes a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the beneficiary is the Participant’s Eligible Spouse; (iv) Ten Years Certain and Life Option, where the Participant receives a reduced Pension payable monthly for his lifetime but for not less than 120 months, and if the Participant dies before 120 payments are made, the remaining payments are made to the primary beneficiary (or, if the primary beneficiary has predeceased the Participant, to the contingent beneficiary). The Participant may also receive the Pension as a Single Lump Sum Payment. A Participant without an Advance Election may choose a Combination Lump Sum/Monthly Benefit Option, where the Pension is divided between a lump sum and a monthly benefit based on whole number percentages designated by the Participant on a form provided by the Plan Administrator, with the sum of the percentages equaling 100 percent. The lump sum amount is calculated by multiplying (A) the amount that would be payable as a Single Lump Sum if the entire benefit were in that form, by (B) the percentage designated for the lump sum. The monthly benefit amount is calculated by multiplying (A) the elected monthly benefit amount under paragraph (1) or (2), by (B) the percentage designated for the monthly benefit. Inflation protection may be provided at either 5 percent or 7 percent: if inflation in the prior year exceeds 5 percent (or 7 percent), the monthly benefit is increased by the difference between inflation and the applicable threshold. Inflation protection applies starting January 1 of the second year following the Annuity Starting Date, with inflation measured over the 12-month period ending September 30, using the same methodology as applied for Social Security cost-of-living adjustments on January 1, 1989, and such protection applies to survivor benefits as well. Any election for inflation protection is irrevocable by the Participant or his surviving beneficiary. For vested benefits, married Participants may receive a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, while all Participants (married or unmarried) may receive a Single Life Annuity, with the applicable form determined under Section 6.1(a). To qualify as an Advance Election or PEP Election, the election must be in writing on a form designated by the Plan Administrator, signed by the Participant, and spousal consent is not required. An Advance Election must be made on or after July 15, 1993, and must be received by the Plan Administrator before the start of the calendar year containing the Participant’s Retirement Date and at least 6 months before that date; it remains effective until changed or revoked. A Participant may change or revoke an Advance Election by filing a new election meeting these requirements, but only if received at least 6 months before the Retirement Date and before the start of the relevant calendar year. A PEP Election may only be made by a Participant who has an Advance Election to receive an Annuity in effect at the time of submission, with the advance receipt requirement considered met if it will be met by the Participant’s proposed Retirement Date. The PEP Election must be made on a form specifying the chosen annuity form of benefit from Section 6.2, including inflation protection, subject to the Plan’s provisions, and the forms in Section 6.2(a)(3) and (4) are not available under a PEP Election. The PEP Election must be received no earlier than 90 days before the Retirement Date and no later than the day before the Retirement Date, and the Participant must provide proof of the beneficiary’s age (including Eligible Spouse if applicable) by the day before Retirement. A PEP Election may be changed by filing a new election meeting the requirements, and it becomes effective at the close of business on the day before the Retirement Date. Any PEP Election is void if the Participant does not have an Advance Election in effect at that time. Elections apply to all unpaid accruals as of the Annuity Starting Date, except for a Participant who is rehired after their initial Annuity Starting Date and who either continues to receive an Annuity upon rehire or previously received a lump sum distribution (other than a cashout under Section 4.9(a)); in such cases, the election procedures at the subsequent Annuity Starting Date apply only to benefits accruing after rehire, while prior accruals remain payable under the initial election. An election is treated as received on a particular day if it is postmarked that day or actually received by the Plan Administrator on that day, with delivery required by close of business as determined by the Plan Administrator. Special rules for survivor options state that if a Participant makes a PEP Election for a survivor option in Section 6.2(a)(2) and dies before the election becomes effective, the election is disregarded; if the Participant dies after the election becomes effective but before retirement begins, the benefit commences on the first day of the month following death, with any back payments going to the estate. For a Participant who elected the Ten Years Certain and Life Option, if the Participant dies after the election becomes effective, without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and before receiving 120 payments, the remaining payments go to the estate. If payments have commenced to a beneficiary who then dies before completion, the remaining payments go to the beneficiary’s estate. If a Participant’s beneficiary is not his Eligible Spouse, he may not elect the 100 percent survivor option if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 10 years younger, or the 75 percent survivor option if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 19 years younger. A Participant who elects a survivor option must designate a beneficiary on a PEP Election Form or an approved election form under the Salaried Plan; for the 50 percent survivor option, both a primary and contingent beneficiary may be named. A Participant (active or former) may change or revoke a beneficiary designation at any time prior to the election becoming effective, in accordance with Plan Administrator rules, and the designation is not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator (or prior to the Effective Date, under the Prior Plan). If no beneficiary is properly designated, the survivor option in Section 6.2(a)(2) is not effective. Article A of the Appendix applies to individuals who were Salaried Plan Participants employed by the PBG Organization on December 31, 1993, whose Salaried Plan Pension was vested in 1993 (or would have been vested in 1994 if service included an assumed period of continued service as specified in (a)(1)), and whose minimum 1993 Pension is not derived solely from the portion of the Plan described in (c) of Article X. The minimum 1993 Pension is determined by assuming the individual’s Service and Credited Service as of December 31, 1993 equals what it would be if service continued through December 31, 1994, reduced if a scheduled termination date in 1994 is reflected in human resource records; the assumed period of continued service is the portion of 1994 ending with the scheduled termination date. The individual’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings are adjusted to match the amount projected under the Salaried Plan’s salary scale as of the end of 1994, with special rules: (i) a higher salary scale is used if the individual’s projected 1994 earnings on the “Special PEP Salary Scale” are higher than the default assumption; (ii) if the assumed service period is less than all of 1994, the salary adjustment is reduced to reflect earnings only up to the scheduled termination date. The individual’s attained age as of December 31, 1993, is assumed to be the age they would have at the end of the assumed service period. Any individual covered by this section and not otherwise vested as of December 31, 1993, shall be vested in both their Pension (determined without regard to this subsection) and their minimum 1993 Pension. For purposes of this subsection, Code section 401(a)(17) is applied in 1993 with the amendments made by the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Amendments of 1993. The determination of later accruals is governed by subsections (a) and (b) above.

The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) was established to provide benefits to salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan, particularly those whose pension benefits under that plan are limited by provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. The Plan was originally amended and restated in its entirety in 1989. It was last fully restated on January 1, 2005, which established the terms applicable to benefits subject to Section 409A—specifically, benefits earned or vested after December 31, 2004, or materially modified in accordance with Treas. Reg. § 1.409A-6(a)(4) (referred to as the "409A Program"). The 2005 restatement was subsequently amended to incorporate the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PBG PEP), effective at the close of business on December 31, 2011, using the version of the PBG PEP in effect on April 1, 2009, as amended through January 1, 2011. The Plan includes provisions for individuals who are not otherwise vested as of December 31, 1993, who shall be vested in both their Pension and their minimum 1993 Pension on that date, with Code section 401(a)(17) applied in 1993 using the amendments made by the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Amendments of 1993. For individuals who accrue a minimum 1993 Pension under subsection (a), any subsequent Pre-409A Pension accrual is limited to the amount by which the Pre-409A Pension that would otherwise accrue for years after 1993 exceeds the minimum 1993 Pension. Article P98 establishes a Special Early Retirement Benefit for Covered Employees, defined as those who do not meet eligibility for the Salaried Plan Early Retirement Benefit solely because they are highly compensated employees under Article S and Section S.3(a)(4) of the Legacy PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan in Part C of the Salaried Plan document. The Effective Date of this Article is February 1, 1998. A Covered Employee receives a single lump sum benefit upon severance, calculated as the excess of the Actuarial Equivalent present value of the Covered Employee’s Total Pension (determined as of the Severance Date, treating the benefit as commencing on the Severance Date and the employee as eligible for the Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit) over the Actuarial Equivalent present value of the Salaried Plan Pension (determined as of the Severance Date, without regard to this Appendix, and treating the benefit as commencing on the Normal Retirement Date). For this calculation, amounts are determined as of the Severance Date, "Actuarial Equivalent" uses factors in effect on that date as defined in section (2) of the Actuarial Equivalent for lump sums conversions, and the benefit is treated as a Single Life Annuity. If a Covered Employee is eligible for a PEP Guarantee, and for purposes of subsection (a), the reduction factors for early commencement of a PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2 apply in lieu of those in the Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit formula if they result in a greater PEP benefit. Article IPO addresses Transferred and Transition Individuals resulting from the spinoff of the Plan from the PepsiCo Prior Plan. All Transferred Individuals who participated in the PepsiCo Prior Plan immediately before the Effective Date become Participants in this Plan as of the Effective Date. The spinoff does not interrupt their Service or Credited Service. Service, compensation, and benefit-affecting determinations recognized under the PepsiCo Prior Plan as of the Close of the Distribution Date continue to be fully recognized, credited, and valid under this Plan as if they occurred under this Plan, except to avoid duplication of benefits. Transition Individuals’ benefits are determined according to section 8.02 of the Agreement. Article PAC provides guidelines for appointing members of the Benefit Plan Committee (PAC), requiring that members be employees at a Band 1 or above level, able to dedicate adequate time to duties, and possess the character and temperament to act prudently and diligently in the exclusive interest of participants and beneficiaries. Additional requirements include that each member should have experience in benefit plan administration or equivalent experience transferable to ERISA plan administration, the PAC as a whole should have experience in ERISA health and welfare and retirement plan administration, and each member should be capable of prudently evaluating expenses charged to the Plan. The Chair of the PAC may seek information from Company personnel, including the Controller, CFO, and CHRO, to identify qualified candidates. These guidelines are intended to guide the Chair in selecting members but do not alter the legal standard under ERISA.

The Plan was amended and restated in its entirety in 1989. The 409A Program Document was last amended and restated effective January 1, 2005, and sets forth the terms of the Plan applicable to benefits earned or vested after December 31, 2004 or materially modified within the meaning of Treas. Reg. § 1.409A-6(a)(4) (the “409A Program”). The 2005 restatement was amended to reflect the merger of the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (“PBG PEP”) into this Plan, effective at the end of the day on December 31, 2011. The PBG PEP document in effect on April 1, 2009, as amended through January 1, 2011 (the “409A PBG PEP Document”) is attached as Appendix Article PBG 409A and continues to govern PBG PEP benefits subject to that document prior to the merger, except for certain administrative provisions now governed by the main portion of the 409A PepsiCo PEP Document as explained in Appendix Article PBG 409A. There has been no change to the time or form of payment of benefits subject to Internal Revenue Code Section 409A (“Section 409A”) as a result of the merger or revisions to either the 409A PepsiCo PEP Document or the 409A PBG PEP Document. This restatement of the 409A Program Document is effective as of January 1, 2022, following prior restatements effective January 1, 2021, January 1, 2019, and January 1, 2017. All benefits not subject to the 409A Program—i.e., those earned or vested before January 1, 2005 and not materially modified thereafter under Treas. Reg. § 1.409A-6(a)(4)—shall be governed by the Plan Document for the Pre-Section 409A Program (the “Pre-409A Program”). Together, the 409A Program and the Pre-409A Program describe the terms of a single plan, but amounts subject to each are tracked separately at all times. The preservation of the Pre-409A Program’s terms without material modification and the separation of the 409A and Pre-409A Program amounts are intended to maintain the Pre-409A Program’s exemption from Section 409A as grandfathered benefits. The freeze on accruals under the Salaried Plan, effective at the end of the day on December 31, 2025, also freezes all accruals under this Plan effective from that time, and the Salaried Plan’s operational rules regarding the ability to grow into benefit enhancements after December 31, 2025 govern such ability under this Plan. Article II defines key terms, including Accrued Benefit, Actuarial Equivalent, Annuity, Annuity Starting Date, Cashout Limit, Code, Company, Covered Compensation, Credited Service, Disability Retirement Pension, Early 409A Retirement Pension, Elapsed Time Service, Eligible Domestic Partner, Eligible Spouse, Employee, Employer, ERISA, FICA Amount, 409A Program, Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments, Highest Average Monthly Earnings, and others. For Actuarial Equivalent, effective January 1, 2009, Schedule 1 sets the factors for annuities and inflation protection, with the 2019 mortality table and interest rates (5% for no inflation protection, 4.2% for 5% inflation protection, and 4.6% for 7% inflation protection) applying for annuity starting dates on or after January 1, 2019. For lump sums and other cases, the lump sum equivalent factors from the Salaried Plan apply (disregarding transition factors), and the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors are effective for annuity starting dates on or after January 1, 2019. The term “Eligible Domestic Partner” applies for dates on or after January 1, 2019, and means an individual of the same or opposite sex who satisfies one of three criteria—civil union, enrollment in health benefits, or other acceptable evidence of partnership—as specified in writing by the Plan Administrator, with no eligibility if none of these apply. The term does not apply to a Participant’s Eligible Spouse, and a Participant may have only one Eligible Domestic Partner at a time. The “applicable date” for this definition is the earlier of the Participant’s Annuity Starting Date or date of death, and “state” refers to any domestic or foreign jurisdiction with legal authority to sanction civil unions. For purposes of determining the 409A Pension at Separation from Service, if a Participant receives earnings during a leave of absence that would count as Highest Average Monthly Earnings during active service but are received after Separation from Service, the Plan Administrator may project those earnings.

The 409A Program refers to the portion of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan subject to Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. The Plan Administrator, which is the PepsiCo Administration Committee (PAC) or its delegate, is responsible for administering the Plan as outlined in Article VII. The Chair of the PAC is the Company’s Senior Vice President, Total Rewards, or, if that position is vacant or eliminated, the individual acting to fulfill the majority (or plurality, if no one fulfills a majority) of its duties as they existed prior to the vacancy or elimination. The Chair appoints the other members of the PAC, applying the Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments to ensure that the committee includes four members with relevant experience and expertise, and the PAC must prepare at least two written reports annually on its significant activities, which are available to U.S.-based executives who are at least senior vice presidents. The Plan, also known as PEP or the PepsiCo Pension Benefit Equalization Plan, includes both the 409A Program and the Pre-409A Program, which governs deferrals not subject to Section 409A, and may be amended subject to applicable limitations. A Participant is an employee participating in the Plan under Section 3.1. The term “Pension” refers to one or more payments payable to a person entitled to benefits under the Plan, with “409A Pension” referring to the portion derived from the 409A Program and “Pre-409A Pension” referring to the portion from the Pre-409A Program. The Plan Year is the 12-month period from January 1 to December 31. The Normal Retirement Age is 65 or, if later, the age at which a Participant first achieves 5 Years of Elapsed Time Service, and the Normal Retirement Date is the first day of the month coincident with or immediately following that age. The Late Retirement Date is the first day of the month coincident with or immediately following a Participant’s actual Retirement Date that occurs after their Normal Retirement Age. The Late 409A Retirement Pension is available under Section 4.4, and the Normal 409A Retirement Pension is available under Section 4.1. The Primary Social Security Amount is determined based on estimated monthly old-age insurance benefits at age 65 under Title II of the Social Security Act, assuming the Participant’s social security wages equal the Taxable Wage Base in any prior year and that no social security wages are received after Retirement or Separation from Service, with adjustments for Disability Pensions and exclusions of spousal or dependent benefits. For Disability Pensions, the Primary Social Security Amount is the initial monthly disability benefit received at the time of Retirement due to disability, or, if received before such benefit, calculated under paragraph (1). The PepsiCo Organization is defined as the controlled group of organizations of which the Company is a part under Code Section 414 and related regulations, and an entity is considered a member only during the period it is part of that group. A Key Employee is any Participant who, during the applicable year, is: (i) an officer of any member of the PepsiCo Organization with annual compensation exceeding $130,000 (adjusted under Code Section 416(i)(1)), (ii) a 5-percent owner of any member of the PepsiCo Organization, or (iii) a 1-percent owner of any member with annual compensation over $150,000. For officers, no more than 50 employees with the highest annual compensation are treated as officers. Annual compensation is defined under Treas. Reg. §1.415(c)-2(a), without regard to §§1.415(c)-2(d), 1.415(c)-2(e), and 1.415(c)-2(g). Key Employees are identified as of the last day of each calendar year based on compensation for that year, and the designation is effective for the 12-month period beginning on April 1 of the following calendar year (e.g., the December 31, 2008 identification is effective from April 1, 2009 to March 31, 2010). Effective December 31, 2017, in addition to the above, all employees classified as Leadership Group 6 and above on the applicable identification date are treated as Key Employees for the 12-month period beginning on April 1 of the following year, except that if this results in more than 200 Key Employees, the number is reduced to 200 by eliminating those employees in order of their base compensation from lowest to highest. From April 1, 2008 through February 25, 2010, Band IV and above applied in lieu of Leadership Group 6 and above. Between February 26, 2010 and March 31, 2010, Key Employees are identified by combining the pre-February 26, 2010 lists of Key Employees from all members of the PepsiCo Organization, as this method complies with Treas. Reg. §1.409A-1(i)(6)(i) and Section VII.C.4.d of the Preamble to the Final Regulations under Section 409A. From April 1, 2010 to March 31, 2018, Key Employees are identified as follows: (i) for the period beginning April 1, 2010 and ending March 31, 2011, an employee is a Key Employee if classified as Band IV or above on December 31, 2009, including Band IV or above in a PepsiCo Business, Level E7 or above in a PBG Business, or Salary Grade 19 or above at a PAS Business; (ii) for each 12-month period beginning April 1, 2011 through March 31, 2017, an employee is a Key Employee if classified as Band IV or above on the December 31 immediately preceding the April 1 date; (iii) for any such period, if an employee would be a specified employee under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-1(i) or any successor by applying the default rules for minimum specified employees, they are a Key Employee, and if this results in more than 200 individuals, the number is reduced to 200 by eliminating those added under (i) or (ii) in order of base compensation from lowest to highest; (iv) “PAS Business,” “PBG Business,” and “PepsiCo Business” refer to organizational subdivisions classified as such by the Company. This method is intended as an alternative under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-1(i)(5) and is applied consistently with such rules. Prohibited Misconduct includes: (1) accepting employment or ownership in a business that markets, sells, distributes, or produces “Covered Products” unless it makes retail sales or consumes such products without competing with the PepsiCo Organization; (2) soliciting any PepsiCo Organization employee to leave or accept a position with another entity; (3) using or disclosing confidential information about the PepsiCo Organization, including customer, supplier, distributor, product, pricing, operational, financial, and strategic information, except as necessary in the employee’s role; (4) engaging in acts contrary to the PepsiCo Organization’s best interests, such as violating the Code of Conduct, unlawful trading based on insider information, or gross misconduct; and (5) engaging in fraud. Notwithstanding these provisions, the Plan does not prohibit a Participant from communicating with government authorities about possible legal violations without notice, participating in investigations, or receiving awards for such disclosures, though the Company retains its attorney-client privilege over appropriately protected information.

The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program outlines specific eligibility, benefit structures, and service requirements for participants. A Participant is eligible for a Pension if they would be entitled to receive one at the time of separation from service, or if they would be entitled but for the vesting requirement under Section 4.7. The amount of a Pension or survivor benefit is based on the Participant’s period of Credited Service, as determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan, with adjustments for inpats and leaves of absence. A Normal 409A Retirement Pension is available if a Participant separates from service after reaching Normal Retirement Age. An Early 409A Retirement Pension is available if a Participant separates from service before reaching Normal Retirement Age but after attaining age 55 and completing 10 or more years of Elapsed Time Service. A 409A Vested Pension is available to a Participant who is vested under Section 4.7 and separates from service before becoming eligible for a Normal or Early 409A Retirement Pension; otherwise, they are not eligible. A Late 409A Retirement Pension is available after a Participant continues without separation from service past Normal Retirement Age, with eligibility determined under Section 4.4 of the Salaried Plan without regard to notice requirements or adjustments under ERISA section 203(a)(3)(B) or Section 5.7(d). A 409A Disability Pension is available if the Participant meets the requirements under Part B of the Salaried Plan and consists of two parts: the first for Credited Service up to the date of separation (Pre-Separation Accruals), and the second for Credited Service after separation, up to the earliest of age 65, benefit commencement under the Salaried Plan, or recovery from disability (Post-LTD Accruals). A Participant’s separation from service is defined under Section 409A(a)(2)(A)(i) as the point where the Company and employee reasonably anticipate no further services or a permanent decrease to no more than 20% of the average level of services over the prior 36-month period, with exceptions for military, sick, or other bona fide leaves of absence not exceeding six months (or longer if protected by contract or statute), and a 29-month period for medically determinable impairments lasting at least six months. Services provided as a Board of Director are generally not counted in determining separation from service as an employee. The term “Covered Products” includes beverages (carbonated soft drinks, tea, water, juice drinks, sports drinks, coffee drinks, value-added dairy drinks), juices and juice products, snacks (salty, sweet, meat snacks, granola and cereal bars, cookies), hot cereals, pancake mixes, value-added rice products, pancake syrups, value-added pasta products, ready-to-eat cereals, and dry pasta products, as well as any product or service under development by PepsiCo during the Participant’s employment. The Plan does not prohibit communication with government authorities about possible legal violations, participation in investigations, or receiving awards for such disclosures, though the Company asserts attorney-client privilege and trade secret protections under the Defend Trade Secrets Act. A Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity pays the Participant for life with 50% of the amount going to a surviving Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner for life, with no survivor benefit if the spouse or partner predeceases the Participant. A Single Life Annuity pays only to the Participant for life with no survivor benefits. A Single Lump Sum distribution equals the Actuarial Equivalent of the 409A Pension as of the Normal or Late Retirement Date, but not less than the equivalent as of the Early Retirement Date for those entitled to an immediate Early 409A Retirement Pension. The term “Service” is calculated according to Section 3.2, and “Vested Pension” refers to the portion of a Pension derived from the 409A Program, with “Pre-409A” versions referring to the portion from the Pre-409A Program. The Plan is structured with articles, sections, subsections, paragraphs, subparagraphs, clauses, and sub-clauses, and references to “hereof,” “hereunder,” and similar phrases refer to the entire Plan. All exclusions from eligibility under the Salaried Plan apply to the 409A Plan.

A Participant is eligible for a 409A Disability Pension if they meet the requirements for a Disability Pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan. The 409A Disability Pension consists of two parts: the first part represents benefits related to the Participant’s Credited Service through the day of their Separation from Service, known as “Pre-Separation Accruals.” If the Participant continues to earn Credited Service related to the disability after Separation from Service, the second part, called “Post-LTD Accruals,” includes benefits accrued from the date immediately following Separation from Service until the earlier of the Participant’s attainment of age 65, the benefit commencement date under Part B of the Salaried Plan, or recovery from the disability. A Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension is payable only if the Participant dies before their Annuity Starting Date and begins on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’s death or (ii) the date they attain or would have attained age 55. The pension continues monthly for the life of the Eligible Spouse. For active, disabled, and retired employees, the amount is determined under Section 5.3 after applying Section 5.6. For vested terminated employees, the amount is also determined under Section 5.3 after applying Section 5.6, and if coverage is in effect, the Participant’s Pension under Section 5.2(b) is reduced annually by a percentage based on their age at the time of coverage, with a pro rata reduction for partial years, except for coverage within 90 days of termination. A Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension is payable only if the Participant dies before their Annuity Starting Date under either the 409A or Pre-409A Program and begins on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’s death or (ii) the date they attain or would have attained age 55. The pension continues monthly for the life of the Eligible Domestic Partner. For active, disabled, and retired employees, the amount is determined under Section 5.8 after applying Section 5.6. For vested terminated employees, the amount is determined under Section 5.8 after applying Section 5.6, and if coverage is in effect, the Participant’s Pension under Section 5.2(b) is reduced annually by a percentage based on their age at the time of coverage, with a pro rata reduction for partial years, except for coverage within 180 days of termination. The amount of a 409A Pension is determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3 (whichever applies), subject to adjustments under Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4 and the freeze described in Article I. A Participant’s 409A Pension is calculated by first determining their Total Pension, then subtracting their Salaried Plan Pension and further reducing that by their Pre-409A Pension (but not below zero), with adjustments for early or late commencement, relative value of payment forms, and actuarial equivalents. The distribution of a 409A Pension begins as specified in Section 6.1, subject to Section 6.6, and any interest due to a delay in payment under Section 3.1(e) of Part A of the Salaried Plan accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid at the same time and in the same form as the Pension, with no interest allowed if the delay is caused by the Participant or if prohibited by an Internal Revenue Service compliance program under Code section 409A. If at the Annuity Starting Date, the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value of the 409A Pension is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator distributes the lump sum value; for Annuity Starting Dates prior to December 1, 2012, a cashout occurs if the value of the PEP Pension is equal to or less than $15,000. Similarly, for a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension, if the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator distributes the lump sum value; for Annuity Starting Dates prior to December 1, 2012, a cashout occurs if the value is equal to or less than $15,000. The Plan Administrator has discretion to cash out a 409A Vested Pension in a single lump sum prior to its Annuity Starting Date if, as of December 1, 2012, the pension has not yet started, its Actuarial Equivalent value is equal to or less than the Cashout Limit, and it is practicable to calculate and distribute, with the cashout made on December 1, 2012. The Administrator also has discretion to cash out such pensions on the first day of any month in 2013 or later, provided the same conditions are met, with the cashout made on that specified date. The Administrator must memorialize such discretion in writing no later than November 30 for December 1, 2012, and no later than the day before the specified date for later months. A cashout is not available for a Participant eligible for a “PEP Kicker” or a “Qualified Kicker” under a “Severance Program” effective January 1, 2018, with the terms defined in Appendix Article E. Any lump sum distributed under this section replaces the otherwise distributable Pension and is considered a “limited cashout” under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(v), requiring consideration of the Participant’s entire accountable benefit under Section 409A and all other nonaccount balance plans, with the full accountable benefit to be cashed out at the time of payout. A cashout does not cause an accountable benefit to be paid before completing any applicable six-month delay (e.g., Section 6.6), and no direct or indirect election is allowed regarding whether a Vested Pension, Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension, or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension will be cashed out. If a current or former Participant re-employs after their Annuity Starting Date and is eligible to re-participate in Part B of the Salaried Plan, their 409A Pension will continue in the same form as before re-employment, and any additional 409A Pension earned after re-employment is based on the Separation from Service following re-employment. Effective beginning with benefits accrued after December 31, 2008 (“Post-2008 Accruals”), if a Participant engages in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of their Separation from Service, they forfeit all Post-2008 Accruals, and their 409A Pension is adjusted to reflect the forfeiture, with previously paid Post-2008 Accruals recovered.

A Participant’s 409A Pension is determined under Section 5.1, which calculates it as the Participant’s Total Pension reduced by their Salaried Plan Pension and then further reduced by their Pre-409A Pension, but not below zero. The 409A Pension amount is based on a method that accounts for early or late commencement reductions as of the Annuity Starting Date, reflects the relative value of different payment forms when applicable, and adjusts reductions in (a)(2) and (3) to their actuarial equivalent as appropriate and customary under the circumstances, in accordance with rules authorized by the Plan Administrator. This includes considering the time and form of prior payments and eliminating benefit duplication, and for Annuity Starting Dates after December 31, 2018, allows the 409A Pension to provide a makeup for early commencement reduction factors applied to the Pre-409A Pension that exceed those under the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors, including any portion derived from the PEP Guarantee. The “Total Pension” is the greater of (i) the pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan without regard to limitations under sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code or the actuarial adjustment under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan for deferred benefits beyond the Normal Retirement Date, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee amount under Section 5.2, with the comparison adjusted for the relative value of payment forms. The “Salaried Plan Pension” is the amount under Part B of the Salaried Plan, and the “Pre-409A Pension” is the amount under Section 5.6. A Participant is eligible for a PEP Guarantee if they have 1988 pensionable earnings of at least $75,000, defined as remuneration for the 1988 calendar year under the Salaried Plan as in effect in 1988, excluding remuneration from entities not acting as Employers during that period. The PEP Guarantee amount is determined using Formula A or B, depending on whether the Participant was actively employed by the PepsiCo Organization in a Salaried Plan-eligible classification prior to July 1, 1975. Formula A provides 3% of the Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus 1% for each year beyond 10, less 1-2/3% of the Primary Social Security Amount multiplied by years of Credited Service not exceeding 30; for a Vested Pension, the amount is calculated based on years of Credited Service had the Participant remained employed until Normal Retirement Age, then reduced by a fraction based on actual versus projected service. Formula B provides the greater of (A) 1-1/2% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times years of Credited Service less 50% of the Primary Social Security Amount, or (B) 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings times years up to 15 less 50% of the Primary Social Security Amount. For Disability Pensions, the calculation is based on Credited Service, Highest Average Monthly Earnings, and Primary Social Security Amount at the date of disability. Special rules apply: if the Participant receives an Early Retirement Pension, the amount is reduced by 3/12ths of 1 percent for each month the benefit commences before the Normal Retirement Date; if entitled to a Vested Pension, the amount is reduced to its actuarial equivalent at Normal Retirement Date, with applicable Section 4.6(b) and 4.12(b) reductions for Pre-Retirement Spouse or Domestic Partner coverage; if the Participant receives a benefit form that provides a survivor annuity for a beneficiary other than an Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner, the Pension is reduced to the actuarial equivalent of a Single Life Annuity for the Participant’s life; if the benefit includes inflation protection under Section 6.2(b), the Pension is reduced to the actuarial equivalent of the annuity without such protection; and if the Participant receives a lump sum, the amount is the actuarial equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, taking into account survivor benefits and early retirement reductions. For a surviving Eligible Spouse or Domestic Partner, a survivor annuity equal to 50 percent of the PEP Guarantee is payable, beginning on the first day of the month coincident with or following the Participant’s death and ending with the last monthly payment prior to the surviving spouse’s or partner’s death, with reductions of 0.8 percent per full year the spouse or partner is more than 10 but less than 21 years younger, and an additional 0.4 percent per full year over 20 years younger. Pensions under Section 5.1 are subject to adjustment under Section 5.4, which applies to rehired Participants whose Salaried Plan benefits are recalculated based on additional Credited Service. In such cases, the Participant’s PEP Pension is recalculated to the maximum extent permissible under Section 409A, with adjustments for in-service and prior distributions in the same manner as under the Salaried Plan, but taking into account benefits under this Plan and any specified plan, where a “specified plan” means the Salaried Plan or a nonqualified pension plan sponsored by a member of the PepsiCo Organization and not based on participant pay deferrals. The monthly amount of a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension is determined under Section 5.3(a), equal to the Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension reduced by their Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension and then further reduced by their Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program, but not below zero. The basis for determining this amount includes early or late commencement reductions and actuarial equivalent adjustments to reductions in (a)(2) and (3), as per Plan Administrator rules, including consideration of prior payments. The “Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension” is the greater of (i) the pre-retirement spouse’s pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan without regard to Code sections 401(a)(17) and 415 or the actuarial adjustment under Section 5.7(d), or (ii) the PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension under subsection (c), with the comparison made as if payable at the Participant’s Normal Retirement Date, and then adjusted for commencement before or after that date. The “Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension” is the amount under the Salaried Plan, and the “Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program” is the amount under the Pre-409A Program. The PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is determined under either (1) the Normal Rule, which calculates the amount as a survivor annuity under a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the Participant had separated from service on the date of death (or earlier), commenced the annuity on the same date as the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s pension commencement, and died the day after commencement, or (2) the Special Rule for Active and Disabled Employees, which ensures the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is at least 25 percent of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2, with Credited Service determined under Section 3.3(c)(2) of Part B of the Salaried Plan and Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Primary Social Security Amount, and Covered Compensation determined as of the date of death, and without reduction for early commencement. Principles similar to those in Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2) apply in determining the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension.

Pensions determined under the sections of this Article are subject to adjustment as specified in this section. For this section, a "specified plan" refers to the Salaried Plan or a nonqualified pension plan similar to this Plan, which is defined as a plan sponsored by a member of the PepsiCo Organization and whose benefits are not based on participant pay deferrals. (a) For rehired participants—those who are currently or formerly employed and reemployed after their Annuity Starting Date with their Salaried Plan benefit recalculated based on an additional period of Credited Service—their PEP Pension shall also be recalculated to the maximum extent permissible under Section 409A. This recalculation must account for in-service and prior distributions in the same manner as the Salaried Plan, but with consideration of benefits under this Plan and any specified plans. (b) If a benefit under a specified plan increases after the PEP benefit for a Participant has been determined—whether by court order, plan administrator agreement, or otherwise—the PEP benefit must be recalculated to the maximum extent under Section 409A. If such recalculation reveals an overpayment, the Plan Administrator must take appropriate steps to recover it. It is specifically intended that there be no duplication of payments under this Plan and any specified plans to the maximum extent permitted under Section 409A. (c) Effective January 1, 2009, if a Participant has earned a benefit under a PepsiCo Organization plan that qualifies under the “Non-Duplication” rule in Section 3.8 of Part A or the “Transfers and Non-Duplication” rule in Section 3.5 of Part B of the Salaried Plan, those rules apply when calculating the Participant’s Total Pension under Section 5.1(c)(1), but only to the extent that applying the rule would not change the time or form of payment of the 409A Pension in a way prohibited by Section 409A. To avoid such changes, the Company intends to make legally permissible, Section 409A-compliant arrangements with the qualifying plan to maintain the payment time and form; if such arrangements are timely implemented, the limit on offsets does not apply. Section 5.5 addresses excludable employment: an executive who signs a written agreement waiving eligibility under the Plan or agreeing not to participate shall not thereafter be entitled to any benefit or increase in benefits from such employment, whether signed before or after eligibility, and such agreements may take any form deemed effective by the Company. This section applies to agreements entered on or after January 1, 2009. Section 5.6 defines a Participant’s Pre-409A Pension as the portion grandfathered under Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-6(a)(3)(i) and (iv), with principles similar to those in Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2) applying to its determination. Section 5.7 allows the Company to reduce any payment or benefit by the amount of an obligation owed to the Company incurred during employment, provided the reduction does not exceed the amount allowed under Code Section 409A, occurs at the same time and amount as the obligation would otherwise be due, and is made during a Plan Year. Additionally, if a Participant has a Prior 409A Benefit paid before or under different terms than an additional 409A Benefit, the additional benefit’s calculation includes an offset for the Prior 409A Benefit, determined as of the Annuity Starting Date of the additional benefit, taking into account early or late commencement adjustments, relative value of payment forms, and actuarial equivalents as appropriate and customary under the circumstances and as authorized by the Plan Administrator. For example, when a Participant is entitled to Post-Disability Accruals after having earned Pre-Separation Accruals, an offset of the Pre-Separation Accruals applies in determining the Post-Disability Accruals. Section 5.8 specifies the monthly amount of a Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Domestic Partner under Section 4.12, which is calculated as: (1) the Eligible Domestic Partner’s Total Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension, reduced by (2) the Eligible Domestic Partner’s Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension, and then further reduced by (but not below zero) (3) the Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program. This amount is determined on a basis that accounts for early or late commencement and adjusts the reductions in (2) and (3) to their actuarial equivalent, including considering the time and form of prior payments. Definitions include: (1) “Total Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension” as the greater of (i) the pre-retirement domestic partner’s pension under the Salaried Plan without regard to limitations under sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code or the actuarial adjustment under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension under subsection (c), both calculated as if payable on the Participant’s Normal Retirement Date; the greater amount is then adjusted for early or late commencement. (2) “Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension” is the amount under the Salaried Plan. (3) “Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension derived from the Pre-409A Program” is the amount under the Pre-409A Program. The PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension is determined under either (1) the Normal Rule: the amount that would be payable as a survivor annuity under a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the Participant had separated from service on the date of death (or earlier), commenced the annuity on the same date as the start of the Qualified Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension, and died the day after commencement, or (2) the Special Rule for Active and Disabled Employees: for a Participant described in Section 4.6(a), the Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension shall not be less than 25% of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2, with Credited Service determined under Section 3.3(c)(2) of the Salaried Plan and the deceased Participant’s Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Primary Social Security Amount, and Covered Compensation determined as of death; this pension is not reduced for early commencement. Principles similar to those in Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2) apply in determining the Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension. Article VI governs the distribution of benefits to a Participant entitled to a 409A Pension and the continuation of benefits to a beneficiary upon the Participant’s death. A Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension from the 409A Program shall be payable as an annuity for the life of the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, subject to Section 4.9 (cashout distributions). The distribution of a Pre-409A Pension is governed by the terms of the Pre-409A Program. Section 6.1 outlines the form and timing of distributions: (a) 409A Retirement Pension: generally distributed as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month coincident with or next following the Retirement Date, subject to paragraph (2) and Section 6.6 (delay for Key Employees). Prior Payment Election: a Participant entitled to a 409A Retirement Pension who made an election up to and including December 31, 2007, and at least six months prior to their Annuity Starting Date may receive the benefit in an Annuity form or at a different time than specified, or both. A payment election made by a Participant only eligible to receive a Vested Pension on Separation from Service is disregarded. Subject to Section 4.9, a Participant who validly elects an Annuity receives a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if married or a Single Life Annuity if unmarried, unless they elect an optional form under Section 6.2 via Section 6.3(a). A Participant is considered married if married on the Annuity Starting Date, with that date adjusted for applicable elections. If the benefit commences later than under paragraph 6.1(a)(1) due to an election, the benefit is increased for earnings at the interest rate used to compute the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value through the date the payment check is prepared, paid at the time elected. (b) 409A Vested Pension: subject to Section 4.9, Section 6.6, and subsection (c), distributed as follows: (1) for a Participant separating with at least five years of service before age 55, the benefit is distributed as an Annuity commencing on the first of the month coincident with or immediately following age 55, which is the Annuity Starting Date, in the form of a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if married or a Single Life Annuity if not married; an unmarried Participant with an Eligible Domestic Partner may elect a 50% or 75% Survivor Annuity with that partner. A Participant is considered married or has an Eligible Domestic Partner for this purpose if so on the Annuity Starting Date. (2) for a Participant separating with at least five but less than ten years of service and on or after age 55 but before age 65, the benefit is distributed as an Annuity commencing on the first of the month following Separation from Service. (c) Disability Pension: the portion representing Pre-Separation Accruals is paid on the first day of the month following the later of (i) age 55 and (ii) Separation from Service. The available forms of payment for Pre-Separation Accruals are the same as those available for a Vested Pension or Retirement Pension under Section 6.2. The portion representing Post-LTD Accruals is paid on the first day of the month following the Participant’s.

An annuity under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program commences on the first day of the month following a Participant’s Separation from Service. The portion of a Participant’s 409A Disability Pension representing Pre-Separation Accruals is paid on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’s attainment of age 55 or (ii) their Separation from Service. The available forms of payment for these pre-separation accruals are the same as those available to a Participant entitled to a Vested Pension or a Retirement Pension, as outlined in Section 6.2, including different options for married Participants or those with an Eligible Domestic Partner versus single Participants. The portion of the 409A Disability Pension representing Post-LTD Accruals is paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month following the Participant’s attainment of age 65. For Participants entitled to a Retirement Pension, they may choose one of the following optional forms of payment: (1) a Single Life Annuity, which provides monthly payments ending before the Participant’s death; (2) a 100 Percent Survivor Option, where payments continue to a beneficiary for life after the Participant’s death; (3) a 75 Percent Survivor Option, with 75% of the reduced pension paid to the beneficiary; (4) a 50 Percent Survivor Option, with 50% of the reduced pension paid to the beneficiary, which qualifies as a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if the beneficiary is the Participant’s Eligible Spouse; or (5) a Ten Years Certain and Life Option, which provides monthly payments for at least 120 months, with any remaining payments going to a primary or contingent beneficiary if the Participant dies before 120 payments are made. Inflation protection of either 5% or 7% may be elected, with benefits increasing if inflation exceeds the selected rate, based on the 12-month period ending September 30, and such protection applies to survivor benefits. Elections for optional forms of payment must be in writing, signed by the Participant, and received by the Plan Administrator at least one day prior to the Annuity Starting Date, with electronic media satisfying the written and signed requirements. For Participants with multiple Annuity Starting Dates, elections apply to accruals after rehire, not prior ones. Effective January 1, 2014, the Plan Administrator assumes a Participant is unmarried on their Annuity Starting Date unless they provide prior notice that they are married. If a Participant elects an annuity with a survivor benefit and dies before the Annuity Starting Date, the election is disregarded; if they die after the Annuity Starting Date but before the pension begins, the benefit starts to their surviving spouse, domestic partner, or other beneficiary on the first day of the month following death, with back payments going to the estate. If a Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date without a surviving beneficiary and before 120 payments are made under the Ten Years Certain and Life Option, the remaining payments go to the estate. If a beneficiary dies before payments end under this option, the remaining payments go to their estate. A Participant may not elect the 100 percent survivor option if their beneficiary is more than 10 years younger or the 75 percent survivor option if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger. A beneficiary designation must be made on the election form or an approved form and is effective only after filing with the Plan Administrator; if no beneficiary is designated, the beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner. A Participant entitled to a Vested Pension cannot name a beneficiary and their beneficiary is their Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date. For Key Employees, distributions commence on the earliest first day of the month at least six months after Separation from Service (or earlier if the Participant dies), except for periods before 2009 when distributions are not delayed if the 409A Pension commences at the same time as the Salaried Plan pension. For Vested Pensions, distributions commence as per Section 6.1(b) or, if later, on the earliest first day of the month at least six months after Separation from Service (or earlier if the Participant dies), with the same exception for pre-2009 periods. Any delayed payments are increased by interest at the rate used to compute the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum value through the date of payment, paid as a lump sum. If a Participant dies, any delayed payments to them are paid to their beneficiary or estate with the same interest. A portion of the 409A Pension is paid as a lump sum to the IRS to satisfy the Participant’s FICA Amount and related income tax withholding at source, with the timing of this payment occurring when the FICA Amount and tax withholding are due, and the classification of a Key Employee has no effect on this timing.

A PIRP Transfer Participant is an individual who (i) was employed during a year (including a year before 2016) by an Employer in a position eligible to accrue benefits under the Salaried Plan, (ii) was then transferred by the Company during that year to a position eligible to accrue benefits under PIRP-DB (or would be eligible if Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB did not apply), (iii) had their PIRP-DB accrual for the Year of Transfer blocked by Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB, (iv) would otherwise be entitled to a PIRP-DB benefit enhancement for the Year of Transfer related to PIRP-DB Salary or PIRP-DB Pensionable Service, and (v) had their PIRP-DB benefit not already paid out by December 1, 2016 (with any such paid-out benefit that the PIRP-DB Vice President determines should be treated as if it had not been paid out being disregarded for this purpose).
